q: How much total GPU memory does an NVIDIA DGX H100 system provide?
How many ConnectX-7 400 Gb/s adapters does a DGX H100 dedicate to the compute fabric?
explain: Eight single-port ConnectX-7 adapters: one per GPU (1:1 GPU-to-NIC ratio).

q: A full fine-tune of a model needs about 1.1 TB of GPU memory. Which configuration is the minimum that can hold it?
options: Two or more DGX H100 nodes connected with a high-speed fabric
explain: One DGX H100 has 640 GB, so 1.1 TB needs at least two nodes (or memory-saving methods).

q: Why are SXM-form-factor GPUs used in DGX and HGX systems instead of PCIe cards for large-scale training?
options: SXM supports full NVLink/NVSwitch connectivity and higher power limits
SXM GPUs do not need cooling
explain: SXM modules connect through NVSwitch for all-to-all NVLink and support higher TDP.

q: Which resource is LEAST likely to be the main requirement when choosing hardware for classic machine learning (e.g., XGBoost) on a medium dataset with RAPIDS?
options: GPU memory to hold the dataset
Multi-node InfiniBand fabric with 400 Gb/s per GPU
Enough system memory for data loading
explain: Such workloads usually run on one or a few GPUs; a multi-node fabric is not needed.

q: What is the approximate maximum power consumption of a DGX B200 system?
explain: DGX B200 is rated ~14.3 kW max; DGX H100 ~10.2 kW; DGX A100 ~6.5 kW.

q: What is the building block of the NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD reference architecture for DGX H100 and B200?
options: A scalable unit (SU) of 32 DGX systems
explain: SuperPOD is built from scalable units of 32 DGX nodes.

q: An inference service experiences 10x more user traffic. What is the usual scaling approach?
options: Scale up to a single larger GPU only
Scale out by adding more inference replicas behind a load balancer
explain: Inference scales out with replicas and autoscaling.

q: 8 GPUs process 680 images/s. One GPU processes 100 images/s. What is the scaling efficiency?
Which term describes adding more nodes connected over a network to increase cluster capacity?
explain: Scale out adds nodes; scale up makes a node or NVLink domain bigger.

q: Adding GPUs to a training job gives little speedup. The compute fabric is 3:1 oversubscribed. What is the most likely cause?
options: The model is too small for MIG
explain: Oversubscription limits all-reduce bandwidth, so GPUs wait.

q: What is the benefit of a rail-optimized network topology in a GPU cluster?
options: It removes the need for switches
GPUs with the same local index on different nodes are one leaf-switch hop apart, which reduces latency and congestion
It reduces power consumption of GPUs
explain: NIC n of every node connects to the rail-n leaf switch.

q: A facility uses 1,500 kW in total and its IT equipment uses 1,200 kW. What is the PUE?
Which PUE value indicates the MOST energy-efficient data center?
explain: Lower is better; 1.0 is the theoretical ideal.

q: Approximately how much power does a rack with four DGX H100 systems need at full load?
Which cooling method is required for very high-density racks such as the GB200 NVL72?
explain: NVL72 racks are liquid-cooled; they exceed practical air-cooling limits.

q: What does a 2N power design provide?
options: Exactly the required capacity with no spare
Two fully independent power paths, each able to carry the full load
explain: 2N = two complete, independent systems (A and B feeds). N+1 = one spare component.

q: What is the purpose of hot aisle / cold aisle containment?
options: To keep hot exhaust air and cold supply air separate so cooling is more efficient
explain: Containment prevents mixing of hot and cold air.

q: A research team needs 128 GPUs for a one-month experiment and then no GPUs. Which option is usually best?
explain: Short-term, bursty demand favors cloud (OpEx, no long-term commitment).

q: Which factor favors on-premises AI infrastructure over cloud?
options: Constant high utilization for years combined with strict data residency rules
Need to start within one hour
explain: Steady utilization lowers on-prem TCO; data residency may require on-prem.

q: Buying DGX systems is an example of which type of expenditure?
explain: Purchasing hardware is capital expenditure.

q: What does 'data gravity' mean in infrastructure planning?
options: Large datasets are hard and costly to move, so compute is placed near the data
explain: Large data attracts applications and compute to its location.

q: Which cost is specific to cloud environments and often surprises teams moving large datasets?
explain: Clouds charge for data transferred out.

q: What helps workloads move between on-prem and cloud in a hybrid strategy?
options: Different software stacks in each location
A consistent software stack, such as containers from NGC, Kubernetes, and NVIDIA AI Enterprise
explain: A common stack makes workloads portable.

q: In a DGX SuperPOD, which network carries GPU-to-GPU traffic between nodes during distributed training?
explain: The compute fabric (InfiniBand or Spectrum-X) carries east-west GPU traffic.

q: Which network connects to the BMCs of the servers?
explain: BMCs use a separate out-of-band network.

q: Which technology moves data directly between storage and GPU memory without a bounce buffer in CPU memory?
explain: GPUDirect Storage provides a direct DMA path between storage and GPU memory.

q: Which type of storage is typically used to feed large training jobs on many nodes?
explain: Parallel file systems (Lustre, IBM Storage Scale, WEKA, etc.) give shared high throughput.

q: What is the role of login nodes in an AI cluster?
options: Provide user access for editing code and submitting jobs, not heavy compute
explain: Users connect to login nodes and submit jobs to the scheduler.

q: Which NVIDIA software manages and monitors an InfiniBand fabric, including the subnet manager function?
explain: UFM manages InfiniBand fabrics.

q: A data center can supply and cool only 20 kW per rack. How should DGX H100 systems be deployed?
options: Deploy one system per rack and use more racks
Remove power supplies from each system
explain: Rack density must fit the power/cooling budget; ~10.2 kW per system.

q: Which facility factor is often missed when planning dense GPU racks?
options: Floor load (weight) rating and rack depth
explain: DGX systems are heavy and deep; floors and racks must support them.

q: Which Uptime Institute tier describes a data center that is concurrently maintainable?
explain: Tier III allows maintenance of any component without shutting down IT.

q: Which item is required by direct liquid cooling but not by air cooling?
options: Coolant distribution unit (CDU) and facility water loop
explain: DLC needs a CDU, a water loop, and leak detection.

q: What should fill unused rack spaces in an air-cooled rack?
explain: Blanking panels stop hot air from recirculating to the front.

q: What heat load must the cooling system remove for 10 kW of IT equipment?
explain: 1 W = 3.412 BTU/hr, so 10 kW ≈ 34,120 BTU/hr (≈ 2.8 tons).

q: Which feature allows a network adapter to read and write GPU memory directly, bypassing CPU system memory?
explain: GPUDirect RDMA removes extra copies through host memory.

q: Why is a lossless network important for distributed training?
options: Dropped packets cause retransmissions and tail latency that slow every synchronized GPU
explain: Synchronous training runs at the speed of the slowest participant.

q: Convert 400 Gb/s to GB/s.
explain: Divide bits by 8: 400 / 8 = 50 GB/s.

q: Which InfiniBand feature performs data reduction operations inside the network switches to accelerate collectives?
explain: SHARP offloads reductions to Quantum switches.

q: What oversubscription ratio is recommended for a GPU compute fabric used for large training jobs?
explain: Training fabrics are designed non-blocking.

q: Which traffic type mainly reaches an inference service from clients outside the cluster?
explain: Client requests enter and leave the data center: north-south.

q: In an InfiniBand fabric, which component discovers the topology, assigns local identifiers (LIDs), and computes routes?
explain: Every IB subnet needs an active Subnet Manager (OpenSM, switch-based, or UFM).

q: How does InfiniBand avoid dropping packets under normal operation?
explain: Senders transmit only when the receiver advertises buffer credits.

q: What is RoCE v2?
options: RDMA over Converged Ethernet that is encapsulated in UDP/IP and is routable
explain: RoCE v2 runs RDMA over UDP/IP; RoCE v1 is Layer 2 only.

q: Which Ethernet mechanisms are configured to make RoCE traffic lossless and control congestion?
explain: Priority Flow Control prevents drops; ECN (with DCQCN) signals congestion.

q: Which InfiniBand speed generation provides 400 Gb/s per port?
explain: EDR 100, HDR 200, NDR 400, XDR 800 Gb/s.

q: What is NVIDIA Spectrum-X?
options: An AI-optimized Ethernet platform combining Spectrum-4 switches and BlueField-3 SuperNICs
explain: Spectrum-X brings adaptive routing and congestion control to Ethernet for AI.

q: Which interconnect provides the highest bandwidth between GPUs inside a DGX H100?
explain: Fourth-generation NVLink gives 900 GB/s per H100 GPU through NVSwitch.

q: What is the role of NVSwitch in a DGX system?
options: Connect all GPUs so every GPU can talk to every other GPU at full NVLink bandwidth
explain: NVSwitch provides an all-to-all NVLink fabric.

q: Which link connects the Grace CPU and the GPU inside a GH200 Grace Hopper Superchip?
explain: NVLink-C2C provides 900 GB/s coherent CPU-GPU bandwidth.

q: What is the per-GPU NVLink bandwidth of a Blackwell B200 GPU (fifth-generation NVLink)?
explain: NVLink 5 provides 1.8 TB/s per GPU (Hopper: 900 GB/s).

q: An organization runs a multi-tenant AI cloud and wants to stay on Ethernet. Which inter-node fabric fits best?
explain: Spectrum-X is NVIDIA's AI Ethernet fabric for multi-tenant clouds.

q: What does 'VPI' mean for a ConnectX adapter?
options: Virtual Protocol Interconnect: the port can run InfiniBand or Ethernet
explain: VPI adapters support both InfiniBand and Ethernet.

q: What is the primary purpose of a DPU such as NVIDIA BlueField?
options: Offload, accelerate, and isolate infrastructure tasks such as networking, storage, and security
explain: The DPU runs data center infrastructure services so the host CPU focuses on applications.

q: Which SDK is used to develop applications for NVIDIA BlueField DPUs?
explain: DOCA is the DPU software framework.

q: Why does running a firewall on a DPU improve security compared with running it on the host?
options: The DPU is a separate trust domain, so a compromised host OS cannot disable the security controls
Firewalls do not work on CPUs
explain: DPU-based isolation supports zero-trust architectures.

q: Which components are part of a BlueField DPU?
options: A GPU and a display controller
A ConnectX network adapter, Arm cores, and hardware accelerators
explain: BlueField combines ConnectX networking, Arm CPU cores, and accelerators.

q: A cloud provider wants to offer bare-metal servers to tenants but keep control of networking and storage virtualization. What helps most?
explain: The DPU runs provider-controlled infrastructure services separately from the tenant's host.

q: What is a key benefit of offloading software-defined networking (e.g., Open vSwitch) to a DPU?
options: It frees host CPU cores for applications and accelerates packet processing
It removes the need for switches
explain: Offload returns CPU cycles to applications and improves performance.
